# N-Repeated Element in Size 2N Array.

@example Four entries, so n = 2: 7 is written twice, at both ends, and 4 and 9 once each.
[7,4,9,7]
=> 7

@example Six entries, so n = 3: 0 is written three times; 6, 8 and 3 once each.
[0,6,8,0,3,0]
=> 0

@example n = 4: 30 is written four times, twice side by side.
[11,30,25,30,2,30,30,14]
=> 30

# n = 2 with the copies two apart, at the start or at the end.
[5,8,5,3]
=> 5

[4,6,1,6]
=> 6

# n = 2 with the copies side by side in the middle.
[2,7,7,0]
=> 7

# n = 2 with the copies side by side at the end: a scan of neighbours one and two apart
# must still look at the last pair.
[6,0,13,13]
=> 13

# n = 3: the only copies less than three apart are the last two entries.
[9,4,2,17,4,4]
=> 4

# The copies at every odd position: a majority vote ends on a single value.
[14,8,0,8,23,8,6,8]
=> 8

# The copies at every even position.
[12,5,12,9,12,0,12,3]
=> 12

# The repeated value is the smallest, so after sorting it fills positions 0 to n - 1 only.
[5,1,9,1,7,1]
=> 1

# The repeated value is the largest possible, 10^4, and after sorting fills positions n to 2n - 1.
[10000,3,10000,6,10000,2]
=> 10000

# 0 and 10^4 are single values.
[0,4,10000,4]
=> 4

# All the copies first.
[21,21,21,8,0,17]
=> 21
